HRA Analysis: ITS ALL RIGHT NOW (6) secured a good run last time out and was running on late into third. She has good manners and with another good beginning she should settle close from the 10m handicap and should run another honest race. BLACK VIPER (11) continues to do things wrong in his races which has been his undoing throughout this campaign. He was very good five starts ago running into second behind Buster Dan and if he can put in a similar effort to that he should be hard to beat in this race. LOCHINVAR SON (5) is a consistent performer that’s never too far away. He ran well again behind Moreep last time out when sitting without cover and battling on well there. CROOKWELL EYES (7) did things wrong in his latest outing before trialling up well in a trial taken out by Speak The Truth. If he can bring his best manners he looks one of the hardest to beat in this race despite starting off a 20m handicap. SELECTIONS: ITS ALL RIGHT NOW (6), BLACK VIPER (11), LOCHINVAR SON (5), CROOKWELL EYES (7) SUGGESTED BET: LOCHINVAR SON (5) to win.

SHARDS ECLIPSE (4) trialled up smartly recently leading all the way at this track rating fast time for the grade. She draws to settle in a prominent position in this race and should be hard to beat from there. CLAUDES DESIRE (3) has gate speed and may look to press forward and find a prominent position in this race from a good draw. He led two starts ago and was just run down by Skip To Me Lou late who has since run well again. HEZA DIRTY DANCER (1) sat without cover last time out at Redcliffe and was beaten a long way there. He draws well this time and with the benefit of that first up run he can run a better race this time. ROCKY WINE (6) was shuffled back last time out before making a wide run into it finishing fourth behind Bettor Cheer. She may be shuffled back again and should be running on late. SELECTIONS: SHARDS ECLIPSE (4), CLAUDES DESIRE (3), HEZA DIRTY DANCER (1), ROCKY WINE (6) SUGGESTED BET: SHARDS ECLIPSE (4) to win.

VINKE BE (2) showed enough gate speed to be the first horse down on the pegs before taking cover behind Barracuda who was able to lead all the way. He draws well again in this race and should be hard to run down. O B LEGAL (1) has very good gate speed and should have the speed to lead before having options from there. He finished fifth two starts ago at Redcliffe behind Major Crunch but was finishing the race off as well as anything there when not beaten far. BELLISIMO ACQUISTO (4) secured a good run off the speed and was running on late there behind Protagonist. He comes into this race second up and is likely to have derived good benefit from his first up outing. AMAMI (8) should get a good run in this race just behind the speed on the pegs. He looked to be quite unlucky last time out when getting back and running on strongly late. SELECTIONS: VINKE BE (2), O B LEGAL (1), BELLISIMO ACQUISTO (4), AMAMI (8) SUGGESTED BET: O B LEGAL (1) each way.

QUEEN TIDE (3) made a break first up from a spell last time out at Marburg. She moves back to a track which she has won three races at and draws well on the front row. If she can work her way to the lead early she is likely to be hard to run down. BETTOR BE BOHDI (1) has good gate speed which should allow him to drive through and lead in this race before having options from there. He has become somewhat of a professional place getter recently having recorded 11 placings since his latest victory. He should run well again and does appear close to another win. LONGSHOT (5) led and set a strong tempo last time out over the 2138 at this track before being run down late by Powermove. He may need to do some work again in this race but is in good form and should run well again. STAY DREAMY (8) should get a good run through in this race behind the likely early leader BETTOR BE BOHDI (1). She has been racing well and should be suited by a soft run on the pegs just behind the speed in this race. SELECTIONS: BETTOR BE BOHDI (1), LONGSHOT (5), STAY DREAMY (8) SUGGESTED BET: BETTOR BE BOHDI (1) to win.

ROSIE POLLEN (9) should get a good run off the speed in this race from a soft trailing draw. She got back last time out and was running on nicely late into second behind The Real Rocketman. BOLD PERSONALITY (8) should get a good run through in this race behind a horse which is likely to be keen to hold a forward position in this race. She ran a good second two starts ago closing strongly at this track behind Man Of Action. TEACHERS PET (1) has good gate speed and finds a suitable race here. She got back in the run last time out and couldn’t get into it in a race taken out by Specialandiknowit. TAKE A CHANCE (4) raced behind the leader last time out at Redcliffe and was well beaten there. He seems to do his best work at this track up on speed and can look to bounce back in his second run for his new stable. SELECTIONS: ROSIE POLLEN (9), BOLD PERSONALITY (8), TEACHERS PET (1), TAKE A CHANCE (4) SUGGESTED BET: BOLD PERSONALITY (8) to win.

MAJOR SLIP UP (2) may be able to press through early in this race and find the lead from a good draw. He led two starts ago and rated good time for the grade there leading all the way. He looks hard to beat. ITS A SPONGE DARL (4) was able to run a good race last time out when sitting without cover and battling on well for second behind Vodka En Ice. He may be left to do the work again in this race but should run well off his latest effort. MAYWYNS ACE (8) draws awkwardly inside the back row in this race behind a horse which isn’t likely to be favoured in this race. He got back in the run last time out and was running on nicely late at Redcliffe into second behind Tiger Tommy. FRENCH BUBBLES (7) appeared to be well placed last time out in a race she made a break taking her out of play there. She draws wide this time and may be shuffled back and will need the race run to suit. SELECTIONS: MAJOR SLIP UP (2), ITS A SPONGE DARL (4), MAYWYNS ACE (8), FRENCH BUBBLES (7) SUGGESTED BET: MAJOR SLIP UP (2) to win.

SKIP TO ME LOU (7) secured a good run behind the leader last time out over the 2138 at this track and was able to battle away well for fourth behind Shades Of Miki and Move It Lou. He draws widest this time but drops a long way back in grade and should find this a lot easier. FRANCO MACHO (1) has good gate speed and shouldn’t be too far away early in this race from an ideal draw. He was shuffled back last time out before running on strongly when not beaten far behind Bigbashash. ALL EYES ON BLING (3) has good gate speed and should be able to work across to the lead early before having options from there. She has been racing well without quite being able to break through for a win and ran well again last time out finishing second behind Bigbashash. A PERFECT DANCE (8) should get a good run through early in this race behind a gate speed horse in FRANCO MACHO (1). She made a wide run into it late last time out and wasn’t beaten far in a similar race to this one. SELECTIONS: SKIP TO ME LOU (7), FRANCO MACHO (1), ALL EYES ON BLING (3), A PERFECT DANCE (8) SUGGESTED BET: SKIP TO ME LOU (7) to win. The two-year-old fillies come together in what looks a strong race. DANGER BEWARE (7) has been super impressive in both her runs so far and will again look to be storming home strongly from back in the field, where you would expect her to settle from the outside front-row draw. KOOKY (9) draws the back row for the first time, having led in all three starts since arriving back in the state. She follows out a handy beginner in IDEN JUST BECAUSE (2), who hasn't been far away in recent feature races against some of these fillies, so should find at worst a midfield position and get her chance to again be in the finish. ANN PENNY (8) is another who draws the back row for the first time since arriving from New Zealand but has shown good speed at both ends of her races thus far. With some tempo throughout and a good drive, you would expect her to be just as competitive coming from behind. BABY CHARLOTTE (5) got the gaps when needed last start at Burnie when a short-priced favourite and looks to be improving with every start. She was a handy second after doing all the work at her previous start, so will be looking to take advantage of her front-row draw ahead of her main dangers. VINJETTA (3) is still yet to break her maiden despite putting together some strong performances and again gets her chance from the nice draw, while SOUL OF KARALTA (6) could be the one at odds if she is able to utilise her sharp gate speed to find the pegs, as she did two starts back. Selections: DANGER BEWARE (7), KOOKY (9), BABY CHARLOTTE (5), ANN PENNY (8)

The first heat of the Dynamo Series kicks off, where there looks to be speed aplenty from some well-drawn runners. SOHO TIGER LILY (3) will be doing her best to get to the pegs, where she can run a very sharp mile when on song. However, WEE GEORGIE WOOD (2) and OUR WILLOW (1) also possess excellent gate speed, so the pressure could be on early, with all three racing very well and consistently of late. The beneficiary of that early speed could be KARALTA ARTEMIS (7), who has really hit his straps at his past three starts when driven with a sit and coming with one run late. In the smallish field, he should get his chance to do something similar here. ITSMENOTU (4) hasn't been far away in her two starts since resuming from a break and, although rising slightly in class, can't be left out of exotics. MR BONDI (6) looks the best of the rest and could be running home strongly off a solid tempo, with the mile distance suiting him where he does his best racing. Selections: KARALTA ARTEMIS (7), SOHO TIGERLILY (3), WEE GEORGIE WOOD (2), OUR WILLOW (1)

COLORADO GIRL (1) has been hit and miss since arriving in the state but looks to get her chance here from the pole draw over the short distance. Although she has been driven more quietly of late, she does possess very sharp gate speed from the mobile start, so expect connections may use that to their advantage here and attempt an all-the-way victory. Stablemate TWILIGHT BEACH (5) has hit the line well at her past two starts and will no doubt look to do something similar again from the middle front-row draw, where she should find a midfield position. STANTON BREAK (2) and GOBSMACKED (8) should position close to the speed with cover and get their chance over the final furlong. COOLANDCOLLECT 4) has been racing well without winning and only needs a good run in transit to be storming over the top of them late if at his best. Selections: COLORADO GIRL (1), TWILIGHT BEACH (3), COOLANDCOLLECT (4), GOBSMACKED (8)

The lowest-rated heat of the night looks to have gate speed aplenty off the front row, where CAPTAIN CHEDDAR (3), AWAY GAME (4) and FIVE STAR SHARK (5) all possess very good gate speed, and expect they will look to use it here. However, all three would need to improve on recent performances to be winning. DANCINWIVJOLENE (2) hasn't been far away of late and should get a nice soft run just behind the speed from her ideal draw. SWEET AMOUR (6) and NO NUKES SKIPPER (7) will be relying on that early tempo to allow them to run home strongly into the finish, where they could take some holding out late. Selections: DANCINWIVJOLENE (2), SWEET AMOUR (6), NO NUKES SKIPPER (7), FIVE STAR SHARK (5)

The highest-class heat of the night, where you would somewhat expect the fastest mile rate to come from. IMPERIAL LAZ (3) will be attempting to use his gate speed to get to the pegs in what looks a somewhat tricky speed map off the front row. At his best, he can run a very sharp mile and would be hard to run down. MUZZAME MATE (2) gets the nice draw and has sufficient gate speed to find a good position on speed. He deserves to break through after a string of strong performances. IDEN LADY LINCOLN (5) does her best racing on speed when driven tough, and expect connections may employ similar tactics here, which should ensure a strongly run race and allow every horse to get their chance. She will have to try to stave off the challengers late. ANGEL ROCKS (1) gets the pole draw to her advantage but would need to improve on her disappointing first-up effort. Selections: MUZZAME MATE (2), IDEN LADY LINCOLN (5), IMPERIAL LAZ (3), ANGEL ROCKS (1)

I found this race the hardest to assess of the night. THEE OLD BOMB (5) returns to the front row and can run the gate like no other when allowed. With no other standout gate speed horses off the front row, he should be first to the pegs and get his chance to run a sneaky race at odds. ALBERIO (6) also possesses good gate speed when asked and, although drawn wider, expect he should have enough speed to get across most of those inside him and hopefully find a nice position on speed. OLLIES MEDAL (8) would benefit from some good tempo throughout, which would allow him to settle better, and could be the knockout horse at odds as the lone backmarker. DOLCE DRAMA (7) is threatening to break through after some handy performances of late but draws the outside gate. DENNY (3) looks the most consistent of the other three Wayne Yole-trained pacers from their nice draws, in what looks a very difficult race where any runner could bob up and win. Selections: THEE OLD BOMB (5), ALBERIO (6), OLLIES MEDAL (8), DOLCE DRAMA (7)

STONE WRITER (1) returns to racing after a 12-month break and comes up with the pole draw on resumption. He trialled very nicely on Monday at Hobart and, if he puts his best foot forward, expect he may take some beating here. TALK IS CHEAP (5), you would expect, may have a crack for the front early using her good gate speed and is suited over the mile, as is COUNT YOUR BLESSIN (2), who draws the ideal gate to find a nice position on speed. Another race where it wouldn't surprise to see any horse pop up and win, including EYE SEE AMOUR (6), who has been running home well of late, and the old girl QUEENOFDANCE (8), who loves sitting off the back of a hot tempo and running home strongly. Selections: STONE WRITER (1), TALK IS CHEAP (5), COUNT YOUR BLESSIN (2), QUEENOFDANCE (8)

Another race where there looks to be some nice gate speed off the front row, with MAXX (1) looking to kick through and hold the front, where he should be suited over the mile. REPETITIVE (3) looks the one most likely to push the button when the green light comes on and has been racing consistently of late. JUST LIKA DREAM (2) has been racing well without winning and should find a nice position on speed with cover, giving her every chance to finish in the top three again here. CHEYS ANGEL (5) will be hoping for plenty of tempo throughout to allow her to rush home strongly, which she is capable of doing with the right run in transit. ROCKNALLOVERTHEWORLD (4) looks the best of the rest from his reasonable middle front-row draw. Selections: MAXX (1), JUST LIKA DREAM (2), CHEY'S ANGEL (5), REPETITIVE (3)

The final heat of the night, where although you would expect ALOT LIKE PENDLES (3) to go around at a very short price, I expect him to have to do a power of work sitting outside SHADES OF SILK (1), who possesses very good gate speed and should run them along at a very even tempo throughout. This should set it up for an enthralling finish for those watching the clock at the end of the race. It's hard to spot too many others capable of knocking off the favoured runners from their ideal draws, but ALWAYS AURORA (5) enjoys the mile distance and sitting off a hot speed, while MONTGOMERY BURNS (6) has been thereabouts of late and can't be left out of trifecta calculations. STEPUPANDANCE (2) will also be looking to run into the top three from her nice draw. NORMY (11) is racing well without winning at the moment. His last two second placing efforts have been strong. He will need some luck from the draw but he looks ready to win and he is worth strong consideration. NEDS BEACH (10) was an impressive winner on Monday here at Globe Derby when he defeated WEREGOINGTOGETCHA by 1.6 metres. A repeat of that run will put him right in the mix tonight. LOCHINVAR RULER (5) and MAJOR LINCOLN (7) are also chances.

NOTHING I WANT (4) galloped in the concluding stages of her race on Monday where it looked like she was going to win. She should find the lead tonight and if she can trot smoothly she should be hard to catch. BUCKLES (6), LOW LIE THE FIELDS (7) and EMILY MEAGAN (3) are all big chances.

HEZ SO ROYAL (10) has a tricky draw to overcome but he is a big time performer and he knows how to win a feature race. He will be extremely dangerous with Ryan Hryhorec in the sulky and he looks like the one to beat tonight. SRIRACHA (1) has a terrific draw after a strong win in the heats on Saturday night. He is a major chance of leading all of the way. TREACHEROUS DAN (5) and LE GASTON (8) are also big chances.

SANDLETON (6) was an impressive winner in the heats last week when she defeated HILLTOP STAR by 2.5 metres. She is a big chance again tonight. HILLTOP BLOSSOM (10) is a talented filly but tonight is the toughest draw she has received in ages. She is a big chance despite this but this will be the hardest she has had to work for a while. HILLTOP STAR (3) and PARVATI (4) are also chances.

HEZROCKINROYALTY (6) is the best horse in this race when he is right. He finds an easier race today compared to recent starts and he should be very hard to beat with Ryan Hryhorec in the sulky. SPLASH OF PAYNT (1) was run down last week in an easier race but if he can dictate the tempo a bit better this week then he will be a strong chance of leading all of the way. CLASSIC LINE (8) and CLARENDEN TRIBUTE (9) are also chances.

LAMBRO LOUELLA (4) is developing into a nice filly after she has won her last three starts. She defeated SAL WESTER by 36.2 metres last start in her heat. She looks very hard to beat tonight. WITHA BITTA LUCK (3) has won her first two starts. She is still learning the ropes but she is a big danger tonight. KENZINGTON (2) and MY ROCKING HORSE (5) look the next best.

CASTERTON (7) was extremely impressive in the Golden Nursery a few weeks back when he defeated CHAMPAGNE PROBLEMS by a half neck. He looks a class above this field. AUSTON (6) will be a big danger if he can improve off his tricky Melton runs, CHAMPAGNE PROBLEMS (9) and ONE AUSSIE (3) look the next best.

OMNIA (1) has a massive motor when she is right. The inside draw should help her immensely tonight. She looks like the one to beat. IDEOLOGY (5) has a lot of ability but he was disappointing last start in a race he should have won. HELPISFARAWAY (2) and JILLIBY BLISS (4) are also chances.

LUSTROUS (6) was fired up last start and was eventually run down by CASH ME UP. If he can trot smoothly and calm himself down a bit more in the run today he will be hard to beat. CASH ME UP (4) has won two of her three starts and keeps getting the job done. She is a massive chance again tonight. SEAPARADEGIRLIE (1) and SISTER STEPH (3) look the next best.

BERSAGLIERE (3) was run down by BAY LA VILLE on Wednesday at Port Pirie. He had a lot of pressure on him during the run and still hit the line well. He is a big chance tonight in this sort of race. FIRESIDE (6) is a big threat after a strong win on Monday. SPIRIT OF SPITFIRE (2) has her first Australian start. Her two trials at Menangle were disappointing. She has won a race in New Zealand though so it may pay to watch her market moves tonight. IMA TIGGY TIGER (5) looks the next best. OVERVIEW: Third heat of the Bacchus Marsh Pacing Cup here following two qualifiers at Melton last Friday as horses progress towards a $10,000 final back at HQ on November 20. Stacks of winning hopes, but ROBLEN RANGER (1) might be the best of them given his good gate speed, pole-marking draw and strong recent form. He led and hung on to win narrowly at Ballarat on October 29 in a slick enough last half of 56.9, which followed two handy runner-up placings at Cranbourne and Melton. He should run well. MONSIEUR FLAMEL (5) and ARE WESLEY (2) are the two Stephen Clarke-trained runners in the race, with the former heading here after a gutsy death-seat win at Kilmore and third placing in a previous heat of this series at Melton last time out. ARE WESLEY (2) has won his last two in slightly easier grade and must be respected, while KITSUNE (10) is perhaps a good runner at a price after a good first-up effort at long odds when fourth behind Cool Story in the first of the Bacchus Marsh Pacing Cup qualifiers last week. JUSJOHN (9), who gains a start as emergency, is an interesting runner and one I’ll be including in the Early Quaddie based off some nice enough efforts last campaign. SELECTIONS: ROBLEN RANGER (1), MONSIEUR FLAMEL (5), ARE WESLEY (2), KITSUNE (10)

OVERVIEW: This is the second heat of the Bacchus Marsh Trotters Cup and it looks a difficult race to sort out. LEANNE LEEANN (8) hasn’t won since all the way back in December of last year, but is knocking on the door for success. She draws for a pegs-line run, and from leader’s back or three back the fence, she’s a winning hope. Bob Kuchenmeister’s mare has been good her last four starts, including last time out at Maryborough when second to the handy Little Miss Valley while beating home three rivals here that reoppose. Happy to play her on the each-way if the price allows. NIGHT FLIGHT (7) is the speed influence from out wide on the front line and is probably the likely leader. He’s not overly strong late, but can certainly give them something to catch if he’s able to find the top. FLOATING MOUNTAIN (9) hasn’t been too far away of late but has had peg runs in those efforts and that might not eventuate here, while LOVE WHO (1) draws to lead or be leader’s back and can improve sharply on his latest effort when caught parked in the first heat of this series last Friday which saw JAKARTA (10) finish second and emergency APRIL SUN (4) place third. BACK: LEANNE LEEANN (8) – 1.5 units (each-way) SELECTIONS: LEANNE LEEANN (8), NIGHT FLIGHT (7), FLOATING MOUNTAIN (9), LOVE WHO (1)

OVERVIEW: HAPPILY (3) is a get-back, run-on type who needs luck in her races but is a very gifted pacer who often storms home and did just that when winning from last at Ballarat on October 29. It was a great effort and followed a close-up third placing to Jilliby Sniper – that horse has won twice since – when held up on the fence at Terang. I like her and she should be going close with even tempo and luck. RIVER STORM (4) had no chance from last in a fast last half at Melton in the IRT Graduate latest, but before that won well at Cranbourne and also did well when third to Cardigan Dan in a heat of the Vicbred Super Series back in August. Classy and a key danger. SECRET SERVICE AGENT (7) has a difficult gate to contend with but was a dominant winner two back before leading them up, absorbing pressure and boxing on okay into fifth in that hot IRT Graduate, while HOUSE PARTY (2) has been beaten as a short-priced favourite her last two in easier races than this, and while she is probably one I’m happy to overlook again, she must be regarded as a chance from the state’s powerhouse stable. ANGELS WATCHING (1) is the other key contender from the good gate and following a close-up second last time out at Kilmore. BACK: HAPPILY (3) – 3 units (win) SELECTIONS: HAPPILY (3), RIVER STORM (4), SECRET SERVICE AGENT (7), HOUSE PARTY (2)

OVERVIEW: SNACK LOVER (8) returns from a break in this 0-49 grade assignment following two trials at Terang. While thrashed by Golden Tribe on Tuesday night, he did a good job to finish in a bunch alongside Madrigal (14 wins) and Crime Writer (20 wins), which reads really well for a race like this. His maiden win was good at Ballarat back in April and he looks a progressive type in a contest where most are fairly well exposed. BLUE MIKI (7) slides back slightly in grade and was a winner of back-to-back races recently at Melton and Kilmore, FLIGHT LOUTENANT (5) did some nice work late despite being well beaten last Friday at Melton and is a contender, while ALPHA CRUCIS (2) and stablemates DOT BALL (3) and TEX GOES BANG (4) look the other winning hopes. BACK: SNACK LOVER (8) – 4 units (win) SELECTIONS: SNACK LOVER (8), BLUE MIKI (7), FLIGHT LOUTENANT (5), ALPHA CRUCIS (2)

OVERVIEW: SOMEONE SPECIAL (8) is a well-bred first starter by Always B Miki out of The Good Times, who has produced top pacers Very Pretty ($299,190) and Major Times ($314,755). She hails from the powerhouse Emma Stewart stable and heads to Geelong on the back of two solid trials at Melton and Terang. This isn’t a strong maiden, and she will be very short in the market. SEW HOPEFUL (7) is a 23-start maiden but has trialled up nicely at Melton following a couple of close-up efforts at Kilmore and Charlton, SONOFPLATINUM (5) just missed in a photo here at Geelong on October 16 and looks set to run a forward race in this company, while JILLIBY UTAH (4) has been thereabouts in recent efforts for Rory Coverdale and might be best of the rest. SELECTIONS: SOMEONE SPECIAL (8), SEW HOPEFUL (7), SONOFPLATINUM (5), JILLIBY UTAH (4)

OVERVIEW: JILLIBY CLASSIC (5) hails from the state’s premier trotting barn of Marg and Paddy Lee and has shown some good promise in a few recent trials on the home track at Terang. He won one and wasn’t beaten far in the others, and looks to have some nice ability. Will lean his way. WHERDASUNDONTSHINE (2) is knocking on the door for a maiden success after back-to-back runner-up placings at Geelong and Maryborough and looks to have the best of the exposed form, quick beginner DANCE WITH ROXY (7) made a mistake when favourite last time out but did run two-straight runner-up placings in early October, while SYNTAX ERROR (1) draws well and has been running some honest races for Eddie Conroy of late. SELECTIONS: JILLIBY CLASSIC (5), WHERDASUNDONTSHINE (2), DANCE WITH ROXY (7), SYNTAX ERROR (1)

OVERVIEW: JILLIBY CONNECTION (7) made a mistake on debut when favourite in the $75,000 Yabby Dam Farms 2YO Fillies Final and then made amends with a faultless display on Redwood Day at Maryborough when leading and charging clear in a nice last half to win by more than 20m. She looks above average and is the one to beat here in this clash for two-year-old trotters. ORLANDO VEYRON (5) settled three fence in the Redwood Classic and galloped late, but he ran okay before that for third behind megastar Verbici and did win a nice race early in the season, THE WOOL BROKER (4) broke through for his maiden triumph here at Geelong two starts ago before being outclassed in the Redwood, while PASTOR JAY JAY (1) draws well and did hit the line nicely late when third on debut at Kilmore on November 5. SELECTIONS: JILLIBY CONNECTION (7), ORLANDO VEYRON (5), THE WOOL BROKER (4), PASTOR JAY JAY (1) 10-UNIT GAME PLAN R2 #8 LEANNE LEEANN – 1.5 units (each-way) R3 #3 HAPPILY – 3 units (win) R4 #8 SNACK LOVER – 4 units (win) EARLY QUADDIE 1,2,5,7,9,10/1,7,8,9/3,4,7/5,7,8 QUADDIE 5,7,8/8/2,5,7/7 Harness.org.au Help Privacy Advertise Terms Of Use Contact Us © Racing Information Services Enterprise 2026 Powered by

OVERVIEW:DISTANT SUN (1) has been racing super without winning recently. She has been flashing home well late and gets a change of luck here with the better barrier. PARIS KAY (7) got it wrong with her manners last start, so we can forget that run. Her start prior was a second in the Swan Hill Trotters Cup, where she ran well chasing down the getaway winner. She is one of the classier horses in this race, but the barrier is tricky. LITTLE MISS MORGAN (9) is a smart mare who won well last start at Maryborough, flashing home from last. She beat DISTANT SUN (1) on that occasion, however, the barrier suits DISTANT SUN (1) here. ZARSKI (4) has a massive motor and a lot of ability, but his quirks bring risk. He galloped last start and can do things wrong. If he’s on his best behaviour, he’s one of, if not the most talented horses in this field. Also respecting WALLIS (2), who let down nicely for third last start. With some luck, he can be prominent here. BACK: DISTANT SUN (1) – 2 units (win) SELECTIONS: DISTANT SUN (1), PARIS KAY (7), LITTLE MISS MORGAN (9), ZARSKI (4)

OVERVIEW:ICANMOTOR (9) is a 20-time winner and finds a suitable race here, particularly with a maiden also in the field. He’s been out of the winner’s circle since finding a purple patch of form late last year. He sustained a three-wide run last start and still battled on well for fifth. He’s racing okay and barrier nine suits. FAKE CULLECTION (10) needs to overcome a wide back-row barrier, but she is racing okay. She was narrowly beaten at Kilmore last start after flashing home brilliantly. IMAGUNNARESTNGO (7) was in a race restricted to NR up to 45 last start and drops back to NR up to 38 here. It was an interesting run, as he seemed to be struggling to keep up with the horses in front of him at the bell, but then picked up the bit again late and let down okay. He’s not the fastest beginner, so he will likely drift back to the rear of the field and need some luck, but it’s a suitable race. OKTOLOVE (6) is one for the exotics if he gets some luck. If JOEYS HANGOVER (10), the emergency, gains a start, he’s a winning chance and would have likely been my top selection. SELECTIONS: ICANMOTOR (9), FAKE CULLECTION (10), IMAGUNNARESTNGO (7), OKTOLOVE (6)

OVERVIEW:TED BEAR (9) won impressively two starts ago at Melton, flashing around the field to win. Last start, he tired after leading. If he’s saved for one run here, he will be flashing home late. LORIMERMAJOR (2) was second behind the smart mare Harley Lane recently at Kilmore. He had barrier two on that occasion, settled midfield and flashed home impressively once he found clear running. He’s an experienced horse who can run well here with some luck. ANIMADO (1) was third last start after leading and tiring in the late stages. He can place again here from the barrier. CATIES SON (3) is third-up here and should be back to near peak fitness. Forget last start, when he hit the barrier arm and galloped, but still let down well late after catching the field. He is a smart horse at his best. BACK: TED BEAR (9) – 2 units (win) SELECTIONS: TED BEAR (9), LORIMERMAJOR (2), ANIMADO (1), CATIES SON (3)

OVERVIEW: This is an interesting race with many first starters. CATCH A BUTTERFLY (9) has all the ticks on paper to make her a nice filly. She is a full sister to Catch A Wave and a half-sister to Yambukian. She is trained by Emma Stewart and her trial form has been good, albeit in slow time. Looking forward to following this filly. ALWAYS BE VICKI (6) is a New Zealand-bred filly for Craig Demmler having her first career start. She has looked really good, winning her two Melton trials. In both trials, she was strong to the line but also under a grip, looking like she has a lot to offer. LIL SPARROW (3) is having her first career start for Kristy Butler. She won her recent trial at Shepparton and we will learn more about her here. FLYING JACKIE (2) has one career start. She got shuffled back at Shepparton and hit the line well for second. If she had been on the fence, her final quarter would have been 27.8. If she finds a good race map here, she could be flashing home again. Also respecting ASHANTE MAJOR (8), who is out of superstar broodmare For Dear Life, making him a half-brother to Pelosi. He’s bred to be a nice horse. SELECTIONS: CATCH A BUTTERFLY (9), ALWAYS BE VICKI (6), LIL SPARROW (3), FLYING JACKIE (2)

OVERVIEW:BUSLIN BRODY (9) has had some mixed form recently when it comes to his manners. He has been getting it wrong and galloping early. However, when he has been trotting throughout, he appears to be near career-best form. Hoping he can settle here from barrier nine, do everything right and be the one crossing the line first. I CHOOSE YOU (6) flashed home well from last to finish fourth last start at Maryborough. His class was on show recently against the top level of the three-year-old trotters when he finished second behind Munny The Munster in a Vicbred Super Series heat. He can get things wrong with his manners. RASTAMON (2) has good gate speed and will likely find the fence here. He performs best when he finds the fence and is racing well. PASS THE SALT (5) is a nice horse at his best. He was shuffled back last start at Maryborough but still let down well late. BACK: BUSLIN BRODY (9)– 2 units (win) SELECTIONS: BUSLIN BRODY (9), I CHOOSE YOU (6), RASTAMON (2), PASS THE SALT (5)

OVERVIEW:RAPTA (4) has a lot of ability when he trots throughout. Four starts ago, he ran an eye-catching second in a Need For Speed heat against a top-quality field. Since then, he has recorded another good placing and galloped twice. If he trots, he is the one to beat here. MOONSHINE LOUIE (2) has been racing well. He hasn’t been out of the top four in eight starts. He can make his own luck and should be able to map well here from barrier two. KYVALLEY REEVA (7) can get it wrong with her manners, but when she trots, she trots impressively. She galloped last start, but her two starts prior saw her trot throughout and win very well. If she trots, she can win. ALDEBARAN JAZMINE (5) has a strong last 800 metres on the clock at her best. If she gets a good trip, she can be flashing home late. BACK: RAPTA (4) – 2 units (win) SELECTIONS: RAPTA (4), MOONSHINE LOUIE (2), KYVALLEY REEVA (7), ALDEBARAN JAZMINE (5)

OVERVIEW:KIMCHI (5) is a reliable performer who is in good form. He let down nicely from midfield to win two starts ago at Kilmore. Last start, he was three-wide with cover for the last lap and sprinted well late for second. He has another sticky barrier, but he’s versatile enough to make his own luck. OUR MYSTERY BET (1) is a consistent performer who will get a good fence trip here. TASTE IT (7) sustained a good three-wide trip to win well last start. She is racing well, but her barrier makes it tricky here. HOME AND DRY (2) was unlucky last start, held up before running home nicely once he found clear air. He has a better barrier here and gets a chance for a change of luck. BACK: KIMCHI (5)– 2 units (win) SELECTIONS: KIMCHI (5), OUR MYSTERY BET (1), TASTE IT (7), HOME AND DRY (2)

OVERVIEW:WHIRILY MAURZ (1) is in career-best form, winning her last two starts very well. She has the best sectional times on paper and is full of confidence. She can win again. The biggest risk to her chances is her gate speed. The horses drawn to her outside, especially HIGHVIEW HAMMER (2), have better-known gate speed than her. She is a massive chance if she can hold a forward position. HIGHVIEW HAMMER (2) does look likely to find the fence here and, from there, can take advantage of a good trip. KNOW THE SCORE (3), at his best, is a winning chance in this field. There are a few question marks around some of his recent runs, but if he can map well here, he may find a chance to get back into form. THE HEATS ON LEXY (4) could map as the horse flashing home late if she gets some luck. ABRAHAM (8) is first up in 52 days and is having his first look at the Kilmore track. SELECTIONS: WHIRILY MAURZ (1), HIGHVIEW HAMMER (2), KNOW THE SCORE (3), THE HEATS ON LEXY (4)

OVERVIEW:FROSTY DROP (1) is a smart filly with great gate speed and general high speed. If she can stay close to the front, take advantage of her fence barrier and avoid having to work too hard, she’s a big winning chance here. BLACKINDEED (3) is fourth-up here and should be close to peak race fitness. She has finished third at her last two starts and let down well last start. If she can map well, she will be in the finish. RAKAROMPA (4) is a lightly raced mare who is second-up here. She let down nicely for second last start and I am expecting an improved performance with added fitness. TRYX VIXEN (5) is a smart filly who rarely runs a bad race, but she has a sticky barrier here. SELECTIONS: FROSTY DROP (1), BLACKINDEED (3), RAKAROMPA (4), TRYX VIXEN (5) Harness.org.au Help Privacy Advertise Terms Of Use Contact Us © Racing Information Services Enterprise 2026 Powered by

A maiden kicks off the night, where CHARLIE PIPPEN (6) resumes from a break. He’s a very lightly raced five-year-old but showed enough promise in his first preparation to be winning here, and I would expect there to be further improvement to come. Stablemates BLISSFULL RED (5) and VOODOO RANGER (7) continue to run placings in this grade and will be looking to do similar again here, despite their awkward front-row draws. REID GRANT (2) hasn’t been too far away in his two starts back from a break and gets a nice draw to settle closer to the speed this week, while HARLEY GLENWOOD (10) misbehaved after the start but wasn’t beaten overly far first-up from a break. He could be the one at odds if on his best behaviour. VITESSE (4) should also be further improved following her debut run around the tight Burnie circuit. Selections: CHARLIE PIPPEN (6), REID GRANT (2), BLISSFULL RED (5), HARLEY GLENWOOD (10)

PREPARATION (1) again draws the pole, where he was crossed early last start, but the gaps came late to allow him to win first-up from a break. He should land leaders back at worst in this field and can repeat the winning performance with any luck. ATOMIC BLACK (2) would be expected to push hard for the front early and has been a model of consistency since arriving in the state. BARBARY TALES (5) is a classy mare with strong overall form. She was somewhat disappointing at her past two starts in feature races prior to the break, but at her best would be winning this with a nice run in transit. MERRYYWOOD PAUL (7) looks the best of the rest and can run into the placings, while you would expect the others in the field to be battling it out for the minor cheques. Selections: PREPARATION (1), BARBARY TALES (5), ATOMIC BLACK (2), MERRYWOOD PAUL (7)

The Bandbox Prelude for the three-year-old fillies brings together an extremely even field. STAYZBETTER (1) was good first-up after 12 months off the scene when finishing second last start and gets the pole draw to again attempt an all-the-way victory, where you would expect she should be further improved from that first-up run. QUEEN ANASTASIA (4) has been racing well and should find a nice position on speed to allow her to be in the finish. Similar to MARIANA (2), who is first-up in the state for visiting trainer Rebecca Bartley. She’s only had the two starts, but her form in Victoria should have her more than competitive here. TWILIGHT STORM (7) has probably shown the most ability of this field but was somewhat disappointing when getting the perfect run in transit last start and failing to finish in the top three. She draws an awkward gate here, but her class can’t be discounted. You would expect the winner to come from those runners, with JILLSTIGER (3) perhaps the one at odds from her nice front-row draw. Selections: QUEEN ANASTASIA (4), STAYZBETTER (1), MARIANA (2), TWILIGHT STORM (7)

The first of the Globe Derby heats, where LIKEYOUFORAREASON (1) will be hard to beat from the pole draw. He was very good last start in the Tasmanian Derby, leading the three-wide line, and you would expect he will continue to improve with more racing. He’s since had a stable change, as has ALWAYS BETTOR (6), with little separating the pair in previous preparations, so draws will be vital come final time. QUARTEIRA (8) is an untapped three-year-old who looks to have huge amounts of ability while still learning his craft. It will be interesting to see if he can kick up early to hold the expected favourite’s back, which would give him a chance of causing an upset. Those three runners look the class horses of the field, with A DRAGON FOR JOE (3) looking the best of the rest from his nice front-row draw, ahead of others who have been racing consistently. Selections: LIKEYOUFORAREASON (1), QUARTEIRA (8), ALWAYS BETTOR (6), A DRAGON FOR JOE (3)

The first heat of the Golden Apple looks the stronger division, where HORATIUS SPECULO (11) will be looking to continue his picket-fence form from the lone 30-metre backmark. It’s always hard to make ground from these middle-distance stands in a somewhat full field, so a nice cart into the race to allow him to use his speed late will be essential to being close enough at the top of the straight. JACKS ULTIMATE FURY (10) is the lone mainland raider for the heats and has a very good overall record. With a safe beginning on his debut from the stand, he looks clearly one of the main dangers here. ULTIMACTION (8) is a classy mare who put in a strong performance to win first-up from a break. She bungled the start at her only previous attempt from the stand, so connections will be hoping she’s on her best manners tonight to give her every chance. JUST TIGER (6), CUSTOM HARLEY (7) and SABINE (9) are all consistent free-for-all horses with good records and will be looking to settle ahead of the more favoured runners to give themselves every chance of again being in the finish, as they usually are. The front-row horses face a class rise here but may be able to run into the minor cheques if they begin brilliantly from the strands. Selections: JACKS ULTIMATE FURY (10), HORATIUS SPECULO (11), ULTIMACTION (8), CUSTOM HARLEY (7)

CONSORT (2) was somewhat disappointing first-up in the state when well backed, after being used early and copping pressure through the middle quarters. From the nice draw, he should be able to sit handy without doing too much work early and be finishing home strongly. OUR DANCE MONKEY (4) was narrowly defeated when second last start after running them along at an even tempo. You would expect she pushes forward here and attempts to find the front, where she should get her chance again to be in the winner’s circle. Her chances would be enhanced if A ROCKN NIGHTMARE (3), the emergency, doesn’t gain a start, having raced very consistently after winning the $20,000 feature two starts back, and would be hard to beat if she came into the field. GOT THE GLOW (5) was well backed and finally brought her best manners to score convincingly last start. Although she meets a stronger field here, she can’t be discounted. KENYA (13) continues to run strong races without winning but may have to do too much work from barrier 13 to get close enough to feature here, while DEFENCE ATTORNEY (10) ran home nicely first-up and looks a good each-way chance with any tempo from the front row. Selections: OUR DANCE MONKEY (4), CONSORT (2), DEFENCE ATTORNEY (10), KENYA (13)

The second of the Golden Apple heats, where the front row has some good stand-start performers, including ROCKANDAHARDPLACE (1), who should ping away from the tapes and run them along at an even tempo, and PADDOE PLUGGA (4), who is having his first start back from a break, but can really fly away from the tapes at times. You would expect the field to be strung out early here. UNMATCHED (2) rises in grade but wasn’t far away in recent four-year-old features and will be looking to capitalise on the front-row handicap. WAVES OF CHANCE (7) looks to be well in at the handicaps on his current form, while FREE THINKER (8) makes his debut in the state off the same mark and brings some handy free-for-all form from Queensland, having had plenty of practice from the standing starts over the previous 12 months. The 30-metre backmarkers in STEPPING STONES (9), MAEBEE (10) and GO THE RED (11) will need things to go their way, but their class can’t be discounted. Selections: WAVES OF CHANCE (7)ROCKANDAHARDPLACE (1), FREETHINKER (8), UNMATCHED (2)

PORT RUN MACHINE (8) was beaten last start as a short-priced favourite but still put in a strong performance in quick time. He may have to be put into the race again here, but clearly looks the class horse if at his best. MORIKAWA (7) won first-up from a long break and, although drawn awkwardly here, looks to have plenty of ability when right. HIGH FROSTY (5) rises in class following his two starts at Burnie but looks to have good ability and may relish an even tempo here. Expect I YLAC CHAMBER (6) to push forward from his wide front-row draw and sit on speed, as he usually does, while QUALIFY (2) and TISU SUNNY (3) will be looking to take advantage of their good front-row draws to give themselves every chance of being in the finish. Selections: PORT RUN MACHINE (8), MORIKAWA (7), QUALIFY (2), HIGH FROSTY (5)

WHERE IT BEGAN (1) will look to continue his winning ways after two very strong performances of late and should take a power of beating from the pole draw, where he should kick through to attempt another all-the-way victory. TAPPY (2) is a handy three-year-old and gets a nice draw to sit on speed with cover, which makes him the clear danger. LETSGOBRO (9) gets the nice trailing draw and should have his chance to run home into the placings again here. It wouldn’t surprise to see any other horse in this field run home into the exotics with the right run in transit, including CAN FEEL THE FURY (8) at big odds, who will look to track the expected favourite everywhere he goes along the pegs. Selections: WHERE IT BEGAN (1), TAPPY (2), LETSGOBRO (9), CAN FEEL THE FURY (8)

The low-class race of the night rounds out the card, where although TUFFTIGER (7) draws the outside front-row gate, you would expect him to take some holding out in the finish. CINCINNATI (4) hasn’t been far away at his past two starts and should find a nice position on speed with his good gate speed, as should BARBETTE (3), who gets her chance to improve, especially if she can cross those inside her to find the peg line. It wouldn’t surprise to see anything bob up and win this, including LALIBELA (8), who could be a late backmarker if there is some tempo throughout. Selections: TUFFTIGER (7), CINCINNATI (4), BARBETTE (3), LALIBELA (8) Harness.org.au Help Privacy Advertise Terms Of Use Contact Us © Racing Information Services Enterprise 2026 Powered by

OVERVIEW: Cracking edition of the $30,000 listed Casey Classic where I’ll side with one of the four Emma Stewart runners in FAIRPLAY (2). He’s lowly rated compared to some of his more seasoned rivals, but I just loved his determination to sit parked and win a good race in fast time at Melton on October 31 and I think he draws to find the top here. He’s a winner of six of seven starts this campaign, with the only miss being a death seat seventh in the Vicbred Super Series 4YO final when he endured a tough trip and faded late. JILLIBY NITRO (1) is a marvellous veteran who loves the staying trips, but will be effective drawn gate one over 2240m. He fronts up here following a good fifth to Ghost Of Time a fortnight ago when he closed nicely from the tail. YAMBUKIAN (4) was super second-up from a long break last weekend when just missing Fox Dan and his chances would grow significantly if he found the front, while BULLETPROOF BOY (10) finished fifth in that same race after settling at the rear. Others can win, including STORMS COLLIDE (6), who broke the Swan Hill track record last time out. SELECTIONS: FAIRPLAY (2), JILLIBY NITRO (1), YAMBUKIAN (4), BULLETPROOF BOY (10)

OVERVIEW: NEATNTIDY (9) has had the four runs back this campaign and I think she’s going really well despite only one win and some average figure form. Last time out, she settled back in the field in a race won by Jilliby Sniper and actually reeled off the best last half of 56.01 while being beaten 13.8m. Two runs prior, she looked close to a good thing beaten when unable to find clear in the straight behind Earl Of Pembroke. Hoping she lands handy in the running line from the good draw, and she should be hitting the line hard late. PISTOL PEARCE (2) looks the early leader if the emergency EMILY VINCENT (1) fails to gain a start and should run well from there over the sprint journey, STEEL THE MOMENT (5) was a very good second behind Jilliby Sniper last time and all his recent form is strong, while KOSIMO (8) might get the lovely run in transit behind PISTOL PEARCE (2) and is a capable pacer on his day. Other leading contenders are FIRE MARSHALL (6), TED (7) and CAPTAIN MOONLIGHT (11), but the gates are sticky. SELECTIONS: NEATNTIDY (9), PISTOL PEARCE (2), STEEL THE MOMENT (5), KOSIMO (8)

OVERVIEW: CARDIGAN DAN (8) looks set to run a short-priced favourite, but things are certainly complicated by his inside back row starting position. His last start was an uncharacteristically poor performance when leading and dropping out in a heat of the Victoria Derby, but he ran exceptionally well through the prior Vicbred Super Series, including second in the Group 1 final for three-year-old boys. With luck, he looks a little too smart for his rivals. The progressive DECODE (3) worked hard early, slotted in behind the leader and ran okay for sixth in a hot The Graduate last time out and the prior Kilmore win was very slick, HANDLER (1) is a horse I think is ready to win and has a good draw but perhaps finds a couple better here, while WHERE IS WOODY (2) has run two good races since joining the Andy Gath stable, including last weekend when second to Refusal. Other hopes include promising mare OUR SPECIAL MEMORY (9), EARL OF PEMBROKE (11) and the in-form EL LAZZAR (6), who has won four of six since joining the Lochie Cook stable but meets a harder test than recent assignments. SELECTIONS: CARDIGAN DAN (8), DECODE (3), HANDLER (1), WHERE IS WOODY (2)

OVERVIEW: CHARLESTON AVENUE (11) has a horror draw here over the 1720m trip, but this horse is flying and was the run of the race in an event five of these horses contested last weekend won by RAPID RETURN (1) from behind the leader, TIMMY TURTLE (8). CHARLESTON AVENUE (11) drew gate seven there, went back along the fence, got clear in the straight and charged into fourth to be beaten just 4.2m. The prior win at Maryborough was huge from outside the leader, and he just needs some tempo on up top to be giving this a real shake. KENNYS SON (4) is shooting for three on the trot after good victories at Melton and Maryborough and appears a chance of finding the top, ALDEBARAN SUE (10) backed up some good form with a barnstorming last-to-first victory last Saturday at HQ and is right in the zone, while WAIKARE ADRIENNA (1) creeps up in grade but has also won her past two in good style and draws for a lovely trip on the fence. BACK: CHARLESTON AVENUE (11) – 1 unit (each-way) SELECTIONS: CHARLESTON AVENUE (11), KENNYS SON (4), ALDEBARAN SUE (10), WAIKARE ADRIENNA (1)

OVERVIEW: Looking to the Bill Collins Trotters Sprint and Maryborough Trotters Cup form here, with the top four picks all coming through those races in recent weeks. So much depends on manners and who steps to the top, but I’ll lean to LOVEMETO (3). He left the tapes well and led initially in this race back in February last year, then quickly went off stride for no apparent reason. He still did a good job to run third behind Keayang Chucky despite racing roughly late. He’s a very classy type who sat parked and finished second in the Bill Collins, and would be very hard to run down if he worked to the front. HOPPY (4) turned the tables on him with victory in the recent Maryborough Trotters Cup, where he ran past the other top three picks in this race to win in track record time. He’s a real newcomer to the free-for-all ranks, but he’s very progressive. IM BOBBY (6) led and boxed on well for second at Maryborough and can fly the tapes, while IMPERIAL MONARCH (7) and the first-up and lightly-raced CRACKERJACK (11) look the other key hopes in a great edition of the Australasian Trotting Championship. SELECTIONS: LOVEMETO (3), HOPPY (4), IM BOBBY (6), IMPERIAL MONARCH (7)

OVERVIEW: Group 1 Victoria Derby winner DYNAMITEDAN (12) fronts up here following his outstanding success in the time-honoured classic at Melton on October 17 and he’s awfully hard to oppose in this 70-79 content. The Emma Stewart-trained pacer turned in a great heat run before coming from well off the pace and scoring in the final at long odds. He’s only early into his preparation and the 2240m trip gives him time to work into the race from wide on the back row. OUR VINCENT CAN GOGH (4) looks a legitimate threat based off his recent form, which includes a really good second to potential superstar Bettor Beach last weekend in a personal last half of 53.74, which was actually quicker than that of the winner! Before that, he ran well in a race six of these contested when fourth to KOMODO (8), who had the dream cart up on stablemate PICK UP ELVIS (10). The latter might be able to turn the tables from what is perhaps a better draw and race shape here. Plenty of others can figure, headlined by THE NAKED ART (6), who returns from a two-start Tasmanian campaign where she was runner-up in both starts at Launceston and Hobart. Her prior form in Victoria was very good before the trek across Bass Strait. BACK: OUR VINCENT CAN GOGH (4) – 3 units (place) SELECTIONS: DYNAMITEDAN (12), OUR VINCENT CAN GOGH (4), PICK UP ELVIS (10), THE NAKED ART (6)

OVERVIEW: Plain and simple, I think Lochie Cook and SEATHESTARS (1) need to hold out BROOKLYN DAN (2) at the start to win this event in what looks a great battle between the horses drawn gates one and two. SEATHESTARS (1) worked to the front at Melton on October 31 and was ultimately run down into third by the very smart Fairplay and New Shuffle, but did a great job to be beaten just 3.4m in fast time. I’m not sure he has the speed to out-dash BROOKLYN DAN (2) if he ended up behind that horse, but he’ll run well either way. BROOKLYN DAN (2) is a speed machine who led and faded in a hot Victoria Derby final last time out, but won a heat prior to that in a slick last half on the fence and is a very talented customer who would be close to home if he found the front. They look the two clear winning chances, with JUSTALITTLESIP (8) likely to get a nice run on the fence in what is set to be a sizzling last half, and ATA RANGI (9) another worth including for the back end of trifectas and First 4s as he returns from a South Australian Pacing Cup campaign where he finished fourth in the Group 3 final. SELECTIONS: SEATHESTARS (1), BROOKLYN DAN (2), JUSTALITTLESIP (8), ATA RANGI (9)

OVERVIEW: What a wide-open edition of the Sapling Stakes for two-year-old colts and geldings this is, with the early market reflecting how difficult and even this field appears. LOUS MAMBO (1) looks set for a nice trip on the fence after coming up with barrier one, and heads into this after scoring easily from the front at St Arnaud on the weekend. He sat parked through the last lap and ran a good race for third – beaten 3.8m – behind Ozzie Tart and CATCH THE CAPTAIN (2) before that and might be the value runner here at around $9 in early fixed odds betting. While he led and was left alone, WINCHESTER BOY (4) won so effortlessly and powerfully on debut at Cranbourne that he appears to have plenty of ability, CATCH THE CAPTAIN (2) won first-up at Melton on October 21 and found the top before being grabbed late in that aforementioned race, while BETTORBUST (7) brings two good Mildura wins and a narrow second to the smart Delizioso at Shepparton to the table. He makes the top four picks in a race where they could all win without surprising one little bit! SELECTIONS: LOUS MAMBO (1), WINCHESTER BOY (4), CATCH THE CAPTAIN (2), BETTORBUST (7)

OVERVIEW: TWIGSTAR (2) is a very exciting prospect for trainer Scott Ewen and the daughter of Poster Boy goes in search of a fourth win in succession to start her career in the Sapling Stakes for two-year-old fillies. All three of her victories have been stunning, including a dominant front-running success last time out at Melton on October 23 when she led and rated 1:53.7 while winning by 11.9m. Her aggregate winning margin so far is 34m and I fancy she will add to that here. SPOOKY MOTH (1) is one of three Emma Stewart runners and two on debut here. She is a half-sister to the Group 1 winner Major Moth ($399,349) and is perhaps the most fancied of the team based off some nice enough trials and the good barrier one draw. Stablemate FARADY (6) galloped early and could only manage fifth in the Tatlow Stakes on October 31, a race which was won impressively by OZZIE TART (3), who ducked and weaved from three back the fence to score. The other on debut is NUDOORA (5), who is the least fancied of Stewart’s runners in early markets. BACK: TWIGSTAR (2) – 5 units (win) SELECTIONS: TWIGSTAR (2), SPOOKY MOTH (1), OZZIE TART (3), FARADY (6) 10-UNIT GAME PLAN R4 #11 CHARLESTON AVENUE – 1 unit (each-way) R6 #4 OUR VINCENT CAN GOGH – 3 units (place) R9 #2 TWIGSTAR – 5 units (win) EARLY QUADDIE 1,2,4,6,10/2,5,6,8,9,11/8/1,4,10,11 QUADDIE 3,4,6,7/4,10,12/1,2/1,2,4,7 Harness.org.au Help Privacy Advertise Terms Of Use Contact Us © Racing Information Services Enterprise 2026 Powered by

COMMANCHE BLING (1) ran well last time out to finish second to Illberidingshotgun at this track. She may elect to drive through and lead this time from an ideal draw and could be hard to run down. MISTA WICKED (8) sat outside the leader last time out and went down narrowly finishing third behind Whata Sweety. He should get a good run off the speed in this race and can be running on late. MADAM FIRST LADY (2) ran well on debut for third after being left without cover there throughout the race. She draws well in this race and should settle in a prominent position. BEE REAL (7) trialled up well enough finishing this behind Tackas Last Dance. He should get an economical run and can be running on late. LUCKY JESS (2) made an excellent debut in QLD last time out when working across to the pegs before handing over to Exit Eleven and wasn’t beaten far in third behind Aardies A Star. She should be able to work to the lead early and should be very hard to beat. LOUARK (6) sat behind the leader last time out after being crossed and finished off the race fairly in a race taken out by his stablemate Toro Loco. He draws wide in this race but should be able to press forward and find a prominent position and should be hard to beat from there. ATULA (8) appears to draw favourably in this race to do no work early. He secured a good run in a stronger race last time out and just couldn’t quite finish it off behind Next To Me. He should find this easier. REAL MIKI (9) secured a good run two starts ago and was running on strongly late into third there behind Holme Boy. He should get a good run off the speed again and can be running on late. SELECTIONS: LUCKY JESS (2),LOUARK (6), ATULA (8), REAL MIKI (9) SUGGESTED BET: LUCKY JESS (2) to win.

BLING THE NOISE (3) has good gate speed and should be able to press forward and find the lead in the early stages of this race. He got back on the pegs last time out and was running on well into third behind Notions at this track in good time. MISTER FREEMAN (8) worked hard to lead early last time out before handing over and running second to The Luvbug. He is racing well and should settle close enough from the soft trailing draw in this race. MAYWYN VALENTINO (5) secured a good run two start ago behind the leader and was able to sprint nicely late to beat Same Old Devil. He then took on a stronger race when getting back and making little impression there finishing ninth. IAM HUGO (9) was able to find the lead last time out and took them all the way beating Dark And Handsome. He should get a good run off the speed in this race and can be running on late. MAGICOL IDEAL (1) has plenty of gate speed and should be able to drive through and lead early in this race from a good draw. He secured a good run last time out and wasn’t beaten too far there finishing fifth behind Littlemickey. DEEP REGRET (4) was able to press forward last time out and race outside the leader battling on nicely there to finish a close up third behind Littlemickey. He should be able to find a prominent position again in this race and can run well. PURPLE PATCH (5) looks likely to secure a good run off the speed in this race. He finished sixth in his latest outing behind Highnmighty after securing a good run close to the speed. VINNIE NITRO (8) looks to be dropping a touch in grade off some of her recent outings. She wasn’t beaten far last time out behind Delightfully Sweet and Always Adorned after securing a good run on the pegs in the run. She should be running on well late. BRITTS MATE (6) has been closing in strongly on another win and despite the wide draw she looks well placed in this race. She got back last time out and was running on nicely late into second behind Littlemickey. VINCENT TIME (9) has a string of placings to his name and seems to be racing well at the moment. He secured a good run last time out and ran on well last time out into third behind Merry Jewel after sitting leaders back in the run. FAVREAU (1) has moderate gate speed and may be able to drive through and hold a prominent position from a good draw in this race. He raced off the speed last time out and was running on into seventh late. He is better suited racing on speed. SELECTIONS: VINNIE NITRO (8),BRITTS MATE (6), VINCENT TIME (9), FAVREAU (1) SUGGESTED BET: VINCENT TIME (9) to win.

LAST CALL (4) raced behind the leader two starts ago and was running on strongly late into second behind October Racketeer. She continues to race well and with the right run off the speed in this race she should be running on strongly again. WICKED MACK (2) has good gate speed and would be hard to beat if he was able to find the front in this race. He raced without cover last time out and ran well there finishing fourth behind Jimmy Bling in good time. ART OF ROCK (8) lands a soft trailing draw in this race which should see him suited. He raced without cover two starts ago and battled on well there for third behind Sheez Got Torque. PLANET DOWNS (3) led last time out and was run down there by Britts Mate when appearing to have his chance. He has since had a break and returns from a spell in this race. SELECTIONS: LAST CALL (4), WICKED MACK (2), ART OF ROCK (8), PLANET DOWNS (3) SUGGESTED BET: LAST CALL (4) to win.

PUMPKIN PAT (7) secured a good run last time out and battled on well there for third behind Martin Magic and Dual Cam.
